title: Lantern and Clock
premise: In the winter of 1917, Theo Oyelaran serves as a battlefield nurse near a river town whose bridge is the only evacuation route before the seasonal thaw floods the valley and the front collapses. She keeps a secret ledger of wounded soldiers and civilians the officers' reports omit, and when the bridge closes for repairs with one final berth left on the last barge, she must choose between her estranged brother, the orphaned girl who has become her found family, and the dying colonel who knows where the ledger could save hundreds. Theo chooses neither to abandon nor to obey: she falsifies the manifest, trades her own berth away, and sends the girl and her brother across while she stays behind, surviving the flood by leading the omitted names overland — an act that costs her the ledger itself but earns her a new family among the saved.
about_author: Odile Amberdale is the pen name of a former triage nurse turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime field hospital records in three languages. Lantern and Clock is her second novel, written in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the northern coast.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In a flooded dressing station, Theo records the names of the omitted in her ledger while officers' lists grow shorter. Introduces her method of measuring the world by what can be carried. Emotional beat: quiet defiance born of grief.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Evacuation orders arrive; the bridge is announced as closing for the season within three weeks. Theo watches officers strike civilian names from manifests. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Counted Backwards
chapters.summary: Introduces Amara, a nine-year-old orphan Theo has sheltered since summer, who counts seconds to calm herself. Their ritual of lantern-lighting establishes their found-family bond. Beat: tenderness under threat.

chapters.title: A Letter in a Dead Man's Pocket
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While treating a dying courier, she finds a letter revealing the bridge closure is partly political — someone wants certain people stranded. Beat: suspicion kindled.

chapters.title: My Brother's Boots
chapters.summary: Samson Oyelaran arrives with a labor battalion; siblings reunite after six years of silence over an old betrayal. POV alternates via his letter home. Beat: love tangled with resentment.

chapters.title: Colonel Vasseur's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. The colonel calculates berths, supplies, and acceptable losses, hiding knowledge of an overland route through the marshes. Beat: cold power rationalizing cruelty.

chapters.title: Ledger Against Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She compares her omitted-names ledger with official rolls and finds two hundred souls unaccounted for. Sister Marguerite warns her that accuracy is dangerous. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Barge Manifest
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The final barge will carry forty; Theo is offered a guaranteed berth as senior nurse. Amara has no claim. Beat: the choice begins to take shape.

chapters.title: What Samson Carried
chapters.summary: Samson's POV. He reveals he took the blame years ago for a theft that was Theo's, to save her career. His labor battalion is slated to stay behind. Beat: guilt inverted; old wound reopened.

chapters.title: Lanterns on the Water
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Theo's POV. The town lights lanterns for the missing; Amara asks if names float. Theo lies for the first time to protect her. Beat: love requiring deception.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Offer
chapters.summary: Vasseur offers Theo two berths — hers and one more — if she surrenders the ledger, which implicates his superiors. Beat: temptation wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Sister Marguerite admits she once chose which patients lived by order, not conscience, and begs Theo not to become her. Beat: warning from a broken mirror.

chapters.title: Amara Learns the Alphabet
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude, Amara's POV. Theo teaches her letters using the ledger's names; Amara memorizes them like a psalm. Beat: fragile joy before the storm.

chapters.title: Rumors of the Marsh Road
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A bargeman hints at an overland route through the marshes usable only at low water. Theo begins mapping it in secret. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Samson Refuses
chapters.summary: Samson's POV. Theo offers him the last berth; he refuses, insisting it belongs to Amara. Their argument cracks open the old theft. Beat: pride as armor cracking.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A staff inspection nearly exposes the ledger; Theo hides it inside a hymnal while Amara distracts the major with her counting game. Beat: terror disguised as domesticity.

chapters.title: The Clock in the Tower
chapters.summary: Town clock stops; time becomes rumor. Theo measures days by lamp oil and morphine vials instead. Beat: the world losing its shared time.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. He discovers his own name appears in a superior's list of expendables. Power's arithmetic turns against its accountant. Beat: the corrupter corrupted.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Flood Warning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Engineers confirm the thaw will drown the low quarter before any second barge comes. Two hundred omitted names have weeks, not months. Beat: urgency made physical.

chapters.title: The Bargeman's Price
chapters.summary: Theo negotiates passage on the marsh road with Odilon the bargeman, who demands the ledger as collateral — proof to buy silence from both armies. Beat: every rescue has a toll.

chapters.title: What Amara Chose
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Having overheard everything, Amara volunteers to stay behind so Theo's brother can go. A child offering herself up. Beat: heartbreak showing what family has built.

chapters.title: The Hymnal Burns
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A shell fire destroys the ward; Theo saves the ledger but loses her medical kit and half her recorded names to smoke and water. Beat: grief for paper over grief for things.

chapters.title: Midnight Reckoning
chapters.summary: Theo, Samson, and Amara sit with the last berth between them. Each argues for another. No one sleeps. Beat: love as a problem without a clean answer.

chapters.title: Vasseur Comes at Night
chapters.summary: Vasseur privately tells Theo about the marsh road's true danger — a flooded causeway — and gives her his own compass, asking nothing now but that the ledger survive him. Beat: a corrupt man's late, insufficient grace.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Theo's POV. Chains go up on the bridge; the crowd's wail. The barge departs without them, one berth empty by Theo's design. Beat: irrevocability.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The town settles into siege quiet. Theo organizes the omitted into work parties, teaching them the marsh route from memory. Beat: despair converting into purpose.

chapters.title: Samson's Hands
chapters.summary: Samson's POV. He builds a raft from barge wreckage, working beside men he once disdained. Found family forming around labor. Beat: redemption through usefulness.

chapters.title: Marguerite Stays
chapters.summary: Marguerite refuses evacuation priority, giving her place to a pregnant laundress, and asks Theo to record her name first in whatever book comes next. Beat: the earlier mirror choosing differently this time.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Odilon signals the marsh causeway will hold for exactly one night's crossing. Preparations begin in secrecy. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Night Crossing Begins
chapters.summary: Theo leads the first column onto the causeway by lantern light, Amara counting steps aloud to keep panic down. Beat: courage as choreography.

chapters.title: The Causeway Fails
chapters.summary: Mid-crossing, the causeway breaches; Samson anchors the guide rope with his body while columns cross. Beat: sacrifice offered, not yet sealed.

chapters.title: Clockwork of Courage
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Lost in fog with three others, she uses her counting and the alphabet Theo taught her to navigate by remembered landmarks. Beat: the taught child becoming the teacher.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Last March
chapters.summary: Vasseur, stripped of command, joins the rear guard holding the far bank, carrying the ledger's rescued pages. He falls covering the retreat. Beat: power's final payment.

chapters.title: Samson's Choice
chapters.summary: Samson cuts himself free of the rope only after the last stranger crosses, then goes under. Theo reaches the bank in time to see the lantern he carried surface and sink. Beat: climax of grief — the berth question answered by loss.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Dawn: survivors regroup on high ground. Theo counts the living aloud, Amara keeping tally. The ledger is water-ruined; Theo begins reciting names from memory for Amara to write. Beat: mourning becoming transmission.

chapters.title: The Book That Survives
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Theo's POV. Relief forces arrive; officials demand records. Theo presents Amara's hand-copied book — the omitted names, now official. Beat: vindication through inheritance.

chapters.title: Letters Across the Water
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter. Letters from those saved reach Theo; Marguerite's new ward, Odilon's rebuilt barge, strangers who were on the causeway. Beat: the found family proving durable at distance.

chapters.title: What Theo Carried
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Packing to leave, she measures her belongings — a compass, a stopped watch, a lantern, a child's copybook — and finds they weigh almost nothing. Beat: theme resolved in objects.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo and Amara board a northbound train together; Amara opens a fresh notebook and writes their two names first, then Marguerite's, then Samson's. Beat: grief and gratitude bound in one page.

chapters.title: Lantern and Clock
chapters.summary: Coda, Amara's POV years later. Grown, she tends a memorial lantern by the rebuilt bridge and winds the repaired town clock each evening, reading names aloud. Beat: memory institutionalized as love; the story's instruments become its monument.
